sections.body: A sentence is a group of words that makes sense on its own.
Every sentence starts with a CAPITAL letter.
A telling sentence ends with a full stop (.). Example: The cat is asleep.
An asking sentence ends with a question mark (?). Example: Where is my hat?
An exciting sentence can end with an exclamation mark (!). Example: We won!
Write one telling sentence, one asking sentence and one exciting sentence about your day.
Read your child's sentences aloud with expression. They can hear the difference between '.', '?' and '!'.

quiz.q: Which sentence is an ASKING sentence?
hints: Asking sentences end with a special mark.
Look at the last mark in each sentence.
'Is it raining?' is asking. It ends with '?'. Find the one like that.
quiz.explain: 'Can I have a drink?' asks something, so it ends with a question mark.

hints: Check the start of each sentence.
Now check the end of each sentence.
'My dog runs.' starts with a capital and ends with a full stop.
quiz.explain: It starts with a capital T and ends with a full stop.

quiz.q: Which mark ends this sentence? 'Wow, a rainbow'
hints: 'Hooray, we won!' is exciting, and it ends with the same mark.
quiz.explain: It shows excitement, so it ends with an exclamation mark: Wow, a rainbow!
